packages/auth/src/server/auth-handler.ts.why: OAuth provider callback handling (Auth.js): the provider adds query keys on its own schedule (Google sends authuser, hd, prompt), and a strict parse would refuse a sign-in the day it does. The owner decided (FUT-4733, 2026-11-11) on a week of observation in the host first, then a separate change makes it strict; this entry is deleted then.

packages/impersonation/src/core/session..why: The payload of the impersonation cookie this package signs and reads back itself, not a request body: the HMAC proves it is ours, and a strict parse would sign out every operator whose cookie was minted by an older release that carried an extra key. The request that mints it (startOperatorBody, startPreviewBody) is strict.

packages/product-research/src/connectors.why: A connector's source config, read back from the host's own database when a run starts, not a request: a row saved by an older release that carries a key the connector no longer reads must keep running, and a strict parse would fail the source instead. The write that saves it is validated by the host.
